question: Which among the following is the highest peak of Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saddle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saddle Peak, located in North Andaman Island, is the highest point of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, at an elevation of about 738 metres. (सैडल पीक — अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह की सबसे ऊँची चोटी)

 

• It lies within the Saddle Peak National Park, which is the largest wildlife sanctuary/national park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, known for its tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests.

 

• Saddle Peak is higher than Mount Thullier (the highest point of the Nicobar group, in Great Nicobar Island), making it the tallest peak of the entire Union Territory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal and are separated from the Indian mainland by the Andaman Sea.

 

• The Andaman group and Nicobar group of islands are separated from each other by the Ten Degree Channel.

 

NOTE

 

• Deomali (Option 1): The highest peak of Odisha, located in the Koraput district (Eastern Ghats), not related to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

• Phawngpui (Option 3): Also called the "Blue Mountain", it is the highest peak of Mizoram.

 

• Kalsubai (Option 4): The highest peak of Maharashtra, situated in the Sahyadri (Western Ghats) range in Ahmednagar district.

question: Which of the following provision of the Indian constitution is not borrowed from the constitution of Britain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fundamental Rights.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Rights (Part III of the Indian Constitution) were borrowed from the Constitution of the USA (its Bill of Rights), not from Britain. (मौलिक अधिकार — अमेरिकी संविधान से लिए गए)

 

• From Britain, India borrowed features such as Parliamentary form of government, Rule of law, Legislative procedure, Single citizenship, Cabinet system, and the institution of Speaker.

 

• The Indian Constitution is often called a "bag of borrowings" because the Constituent Assembly adapted features from various countries' constitutions while suiting them to Indian conditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution, while the Fundamental Duties and the concept of Planning Commission were inspired by the erstwhile USSR (now Russia).

 

• The federal system with a strong centre was influenced by the Government of India Act, 1935.

 

NOTE

 

• Legislative procedure (Option 2): Borrowed from Britain, along with the parliamentary system of government.

 

• Bicameralism (Option 3): The two-House legislature (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) is a British-inspired feature.

 

• Rule of law (Option 4): A core principle of the British constitutional system, adopted into the Indian Constitution.

question: Certain plants have green and tender stems. They are usually short and may not have many branches. What are they called as?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Herbs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Herbs are small plants with a green and tender (soft) stem. They are usually short in height and may have few or no branches. (शाकीय पौधे — हरा और कोमल तना)

 

• Herbs generally have a short life span and complete their life cycle within one or two seasons; common examples include tomato, wheat, mint, and coriander.

 

• Since the stem is soft and green, herbs cannot grow very tall or support heavy branches, unlike shrubs and trees.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shrubs are medium-sized, bushy plants with a hard, woody stem that branches out near the base (e.g., rose, henna).

 

• Trees are tall plants with a hard, woody, and thick main stem (trunk) that branches out well above the ground (e.g., mango, neem).

 

NOTE

 

• Shrubs (Option 2): Have hard, woody stems that branch out near the ground, unlike the soft green stems of herbs.

 

• Trees (Option 3): Tall plants with a hard, woody trunk, quite unlike the short, tender-stemmed herbs described in the question.

 

• Creepers (Option 4): Plants with weak stems that cannot stand upright and instead spread/creep along the ground (e.g., pumpkin, watermelon).

question: On learning about the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, ______ expressed the pain and anger of the country by renouncing his knighthood.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindranath Tagore, who had been knighted ("Sir") by the British in 1915, renounced his knighthood in May 1919 in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar). (रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर — नाइटहुड की उपाधि त्याग दी)

 

• In his letter to Viceroy Lord Chelmsford, Tagore wrote that the time had come when badges of honour make the humiliation of the people glaringly incongruous.

 

• Tagore had earlier been awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his work "Gitanjali".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre was carried out under the orders of General Reginald Dyer, and it became a turning point that galvanized the Indian independence movement.

 

• Tagore also composed the national anthems of both India ("Jana Gana Mana") and Bangladesh ("Amar Shonar Bangla").

 

NOTE

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 1): Known as the "Grand Old Man of India"; founder of the theory of "Drain of Wealth" and author of "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"; he did not hold a knighthood to renounce.

 

• Badruddin Tyabji (Option 2): Third president of the Indian National Congress and the first Indian barrister of the Bombay High Court; not associated with renouncing a knighthood over Jallianwala Bagh.

 

• Surendranath Banerji (Option 4): Founder of the Indian National Association and a prominent moderate leader of the Congress; not connected with renouncing knighthood in this context.

question: A megabyte (MB) consists of 1024 ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kilobytes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In computer memory measurement (binary system), 1 Megabyte (MB) = 1024 Kilobytes (KB). (1 मेगाबाइट = 1024 किलोबाइट)

 

• Similarly, 1 Kilobyte (KB) = 1024 Bytes, and 1 Gigabyte (GB) = 1024 Megabytes.

 

• This hierarchy continues upward: 1 Terabyte (TB) = 1024 Gigabytes, and 1 Petabyte (PB) = 1024 Terabytes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The smallest unit of computer memory is a bit (binary digit), and 8 bits make 1 byte.

 

• The complete standard hierarchy is: Bit → Byte → Kilobyte → Megabyte → Gigabyte → Terabyte → Petabyte → Exabyte.

 

NOTE

 

• Gigabytes (Option 1): A gigabyte is a much larger unit than a megabyte (1 GB = 1024 MB), so a megabyte cannot be made up of gigabytes.

 

• Terabytes (Option 3): An even larger unit than a gigabyte (1 TB = 1024 GB); far too large to be a subunit of a megabyte.

 

• Bytes (Option 4): 1 Megabyte equals 1024 × 1024 = 1,048,576 bytes, not 1024 bytes — 1024 bytes instead makes up 1 Kilobyte.

question:
Which of the following pairs of "term – definition" is correct?
I. Strait – a narrow strip of land joining two landmasses
II. Isthmus – a narrow passage of water connecting two large water bodies
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Strait is actually a narrow passage of water connecting two large water bodies (e.g., two seas), not a strip of land — so Statement I is incorrect. (जलडमरूमध्य — दो जलाशयों को जोड़ने वाला संकरा जल मार्ग)

 

• An Isthmus is actually a narrow strip of land connecting two larger landmasses, not a water passage — so Statement II is incorrect.

 

• The definitions in the question have been swapped — the definition given for "Strait" actually describes an isthmus, and the definition given for "Isthmus" actually describes a strait.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Example of a strait: the Palk Strait, separating India and Sri Lanka.

 

• Example of an isthmus: the Isthmus of Panama, connecting North and South America.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement II (Isthmus) is also wrongly defined, not just Statement I.

 

• Both I and II (Option 2): Incorrect, because both definitions as given are actually swapped/wrong, not correct.

 

• Only I (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement I (Strait) is wrongly defined, not correctly defined.

question: Which of the following is NOT a play written by Shakespeare?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Candlestand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The Candlestand" is not a play written by William Shakespeare — no such work exists in his known canon of plays.

 

• William Shakespeare (1564–1616), the celebrated English playwright and poet, wrote 37–39 plays including tragedies, comedies, and histories, along with 154 sonnets. (विलियम शेक्सपियर — प्रसिद्ध अंग्रेज़ी नाटककार)

 

• Antony and Cleopatra, The Comedy of Errors, and Othello are all authentic and well-known plays written by Shakespeare.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shakespeare's major tragedies include Hamlet, Macbeth, King Lear, and Othello — together often called his "Big Four" tragedies.

 

• His famous comedies include A Midsummer Night's Dream, Twelfth Night, and The Comedy of Errors.

 

NOTE

 

• Antony and Cleopatra (Option 1): A genuine tragedy by Shakespeare, based on the relationship between the Roman general Mark Antony and the Egyptian queen Cleopatra.

 

• The Comedy of Errors (Option 2): One of Shakespeare's early comedies, known for its plot involving mistaken identities of two sets of twins.

 

• Othello (Option 4): A major tragedy by Shakespeare centred on the Moorish general Othello and the villain Iago.

question: In MS-Excel 365 which of the following shortcut is used to copy the contents and format of the topmost cell of a selected range into the cells below?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ctrl + D is the "Fill Down" shortcut in MS-Excel, used to copy the contents and formatting of the topmost cell of a selected range into all the cells below it. (Ctrl + D — ऊपर के सेल की सामग्री नीचे भरना)

 

• To use it, the user selects a range of cells (including the source cell at the top) and presses Ctrl + D; Excel then fills the entire selection with the top cell's content and format.

 

• This is a quick alternative to manually copying (Ctrl + C) and pasting (Ctrl + V) into multiple cells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The corresponding shortcut for filling a selection with the content of the leftmost cell (copying rightward) is Ctrl + R ("Fill Right").

 

• Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V remain the general shortcuts for Copy and Paste in Excel and most other applications.

 

NOTE

 

• Alt + D (Option 1): Not a standard Excel fill/copy shortcut; Alt is generally used to access the Ribbon menu shortcuts (KeyTips).

 

• Alt + C (Option 3): Not a recognised Excel shortcut for this fill-down function.

 

• Ctrl + C (Option 4): This is the general "Copy" shortcut (copies the selected cell to the clipboard), not the specific fill-down-into-range shortcut.

question: Which dance is performed by women of Maharashtra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lavani dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lavani is a traditional dance form performed by women of Maharashtra, characterised by powerful rhythm and sung to the beats of the dholki (a percussion instrument). (लावणी — महाराष्ट्र की महिलाओं का पारंपरिक नृत्य)

 

• The word "Lavani" is believed to be derived from "Lavanya", meaning beauty, and the dance is traditionally performed wearing a nine-yard saree (nauvari).

 

• Lavani songs traditionally deal with themes such as romance, society, and politics, and the dance is closely associated with the folk theatre form "Tamasha".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Maharashtra include Koli (fisherfolk dance) and Dhangari Gaja.

 

• Lavani has also been popularised through Marathi and Bollywood cinema.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghoomer dance (Option 1): A traditional folk dance performed by women in Rajasthan, especially by the Bhil tribe and Rajput women.

 

• Bihu dance (Option 2): A folk dance associated with the Bihu festival of Assam, performed by both men and women.

 

• Bhangra dance (Option 4): A vibrant folk dance from Punjab, traditionally performed by men during the harvest festival of Baisakhi.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with the special provision with respect to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 371.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 371 of the Indian Constitution contains special provisions with respect to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat. (अनुच्छेद 371 — महाराष्ट्र और गुजरात हेतु विशेष प्रावधान)

 

• Under this Article, the Governor has special responsibility for the establishment of separate development boards for Vidarbha, Marathwada, and the rest of Maharashtra, and for Saurashtra, Kutch, and the rest of Gujarat.

 

• Articles 371 to 371-J collectively deal with special provisions for various states such as Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, and Karnataka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 371-A deals with special provisions for Nagaland, while Article 371-C deals with Manipur.

 

• These special provisions were inserted through various constitutional amendments to address the unique historical, social, and administrative needs of specific states.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 386 (Option 2): No such substantive article exists in the Constitution's operative special-provisions scheme relevant here.

 

• Article 377 (Option 3): Relates to the continuance of orders relating to persons who have been transferred to the service of a State (miscellaneous provision), not to Maharashtra and Gujarat.

 

• Article 380 (Option 4): Not related to the special provisions for Maharashtra and Gujarat.

question: What is the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A loan Scheme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) was launched on 8 April 2015 to provide collateral-free loans up to ₹10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises. (प्रधानमंत्री मुद्रा योजना — ऋण/लोन योजना)

 

• Loans under PMMY are extended by banks, NBFCs, and MFIs, and are categorised into three types: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).

 

• The scheme is implemented through MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) Bank, set up under the Ministry of Finance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMMY primarily aims to fund small business units and self-employed individuals who otherwise lack access to formal institutional credit.

 

• A newer category, Tarun Plus, was later added for loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have successfully availed and repaid loans under the Tarun category.

 

NOTE

 

• A scheme for free medicines (Option 2): This describes schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), not the Mudra Yojana.

 

• An insurance Scheme (Option 3): Insurance schemes include Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana and Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, not Mudra Yojana.

 

• An employment Scheme (Option 4): Employment-focused schemes include MGNREGA and Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana, not Mudra Yojana.

question: The ‘Karmayoddha Granth’ book was released by which of the following politician?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amit Shah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Amit Shah, the Union Home Minister, released the book ‘Karmayoddha Granth’, which is based on the life and works of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. (अमित शाह — कर्मयोद्धा ग्रंथ का विमोचन)

 

• The book was released ahead of the Prime Minister's birthday and chronicles his journey and governance initiatives.

 

• The release was covered through an official press release by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), confirming Amit Shah as the releasing dignitary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amit Shah has held the portfolios of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation in the Government of India.

 

• Several biographical books and compilations on PM Modi's life and works have been released by senior BJP leaders on various occasions.

 

NOTE

 

• Rahul Gandhi (Option 2): Senior Congress leader and former Congress President; not associated with releasing this book.

 

• Nitin Gadkari (Option 3): Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways; not the one who released ‘Karmayoddha Granth’.

 

• Smriti Irani (Option 4): Union Minister for Women and Child Development (at the time); not associated with releasing this particular book.

question: Which of the following is the largest peninsular river in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godavari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Godavari is the largest peninsular river of India, with a length of about 1,465 km, and is often referred to as the "Dakshin Ganga" (Ganga of the South). (गोदावरी — दक्षिण गंगा)

 

• It originates near Trimbakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra and flows through Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha before draining into the Bay of Bengal.

 

• The Godavari basin is the largest river basin among the peninsular rivers, covering parts of several central and southern Indian states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major tributaries of the Godavari include the Purna, Manjira, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Indravati, and Sabari.

 

• The Godavari, along with the Krishna, forms one of the largest deltas on the eastern coast of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Krishna (Option 1): The second-largest peninsular river of India, originating near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra and flowing into the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Kaveri (Option 3): A relatively smaller but important peninsular river, originating at Talakaveri in Karnataka, known for the Sivasamudram Falls and its role in the Karnataka–Tamil Nadu water dispute.

 

• Mahanadi (Option 4): A peninsular river of central-eastern India, originating in Chhattisgarh and known for the Hirakud Dam.

question:
Which of the following pairs of 'elements – valency' is correct?
I. Boron – 2
II. Fluorine – 3
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Boron has an atomic number of 5 (electronic configuration 2, 3), giving it a valency of 3, not 2 as stated in Statement I. (बोरॉन की संयोजकता 3 है)

 

• Fluorine has an atomic number of 9 (electronic configuration 2, 7), giving it a valency of 1, not 3 as stated in Statement II — it needs to gain just one electron to complete its octet.

 

• Since neither of the given element–valency pairs is correct, the answer is "Neither I nor II".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Valency is determined by the number of electrons in the outermost shell that an atom needs to gain, lose, or share to attain a stable (octet) configuration.

 

• Common valencies: Hydrogen and Fluorine = 1, Oxygen = 2, Nitrogen and Boron = 3, Carbon and Silicon = 4.

 

NOTE

 

• Both I and II (Option 2): Incorrect, since neither pair correctly states the actual valency of the element.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Fluorine's valency is 1, not 3, so Statement II is also wrong.

 

• Only I (Option 4): Incorrect, since Boron's valency is 3, not 2, so Statement I is also wrong.

question:
Which of the following assumptions is made to determine the level of aggregate demand for final goods in the economy?
I. A constant final goods price and constant rate of interest over short run are assumed.
II. The aggregate supply is assumed to be perfectly elastic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Keynesian short-run income-determination model, the level of aggregate demand (AD) for final goods is derived under the assumption of a constant final goods price level and a constant rate of interest over the short run. (समष्टि माँग — मूल्य स्तर और ब्याज दर स्थिर मानी जाती है)

 

• The model also assumes that aggregate supply (AS) is perfectly elastic in the short run — meaning producers are willing to supply any quantity demanded at the given (fixed) price level, so output is determined purely by the level of demand.

 

• These simplifying assumptions allow economists to focus on how demand-side factors (consumption, investment, government spending) determine the equilibrium level of national income in the short run.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This framework underlies the derivation of the Aggregate Demand (AD) = Aggregate Supply (AS) equilibrium condition used in the simple Keynesian cross model.

 

• In the long run, by contrast, prices and interest rates are allowed to vary, and aggregate supply is not treated as perfectly elastic.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incomplete, as Statement I (constant price and interest rate) is also a valid assumption of the model.

 

• Only I (Option 2): Incomplete, as Statement II (perfectly elastic aggregate supply) is also a valid assumption of the model.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, since both statements correctly describe standard assumptions of the short-run aggregate demand framework.

question:
Who among the following Indian athletes won a Gold medal in 2022 Common Wealth Games?
I. Saurav Ghosal
II. Anshu Malik
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saurav Ghosal won the bronze medal in men's singles squash at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games — becoming the first Indian to win an individual medal in squash at the Commonwealth Games — but this was not a gold medal. (सौरव घोषाल — कांस्य पदक, स्वर्ण नहीं)

 

• Anshu Malik won the silver medal in the women's freestyle 57 kg wrestling event at the same Games, losing the final to Nigeria's Odunayo Adekuoroye — this was also not a gold medal.

 

• Since neither athlete won a gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, the correct answer is "Neither I nor II".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India finished 4th in the overall medal tally at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games, with 22 gold, 16 silver, and 23 bronze medals.

 

• Notable Indian gold medallists at CWG 2022 include weightlifters Mirabai Chanu and Jeremy Lalrinnunga, and the men's Table Tennis team.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since Saurav Ghosal won bronze, not gold.

 

• Both I and II (Option 2): Incorrect, as neither athlete won a gold medal.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, since Anshu Malik won silver, not gold.

question:
Which of the following pairs of "sports – medal" is correct regarding performance of India in 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games?
I. Javelin Throw – Silver
II. Men’s Hockey – Gold
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, Neeraj Chopra won the Gold medal in Javelin Throw, not a Silver medal as stated in Statement I — this was India's first-ever Olympic gold in athletics. (नीरज चोपड़ा — भाला फेंक में स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• The Indian Men's Hockey team won the Bronze medal at Tokyo 2020, defeating Germany in the bronze-medal match, not a Gold medal as stated in Statement II — this ended India's 41-year wait for an Olympic hockey medal.

 

• Since both statements misstate the actual medals won, the correct answer is "Neither I nor II".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's overall tally at Tokyo 2020 was 1 Gold, 2 Silver, and 4 Bronze medals — its best-ever performance at a single Olympic Games at that time.

 

• The Indian women's hockey team also had a historic run at Tokyo 2020, finishing fourth after narrowly losing the bronze-medal match.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, since India won Bronze (not Gold) in Men's Hockey.

 

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since neither statement correctly states the medal actually won.

 

• Only I (Option 4): Incorrect, since India won Gold (not Silver) in Javelin Throw.

question: The book titled ‘The Immortals of Meluha' is written by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amish Tripathi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ‘The Immortals of Meluha’ (2010) is the first book of the Shiva Trilogy, written by Indian author Amish Tripathi. (अमीश त्रिपाठी — शिव त्रयी के लेखक)

 

• The Shiva Trilogy reimagines the Hindu deity Shiva as a mortal man from Tibet, and comprises three books: ‘The Immortals of Meluha’, ‘The Secret of the Nagas’, and ‘The Oath of the Vayuputras’.

 

• Amish Tripathi is also known for the "Ram Chandra Series" of mythological fiction novels based on the Ramayana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amish Tripathi has also served in a diplomatic role as Director of the Nehru Centre, London, and later as India's High Commissioner to Bahrain.

 

• His books are noted for blending Indian mythology with fast-paced fiction narrative style, making them widely popular bestsellers.

 

NOTE

 

• Sushil Kumar (Option 1): An Indian wrestler and Olympic medallist, not an author of this book.

 

• Devdutt Pattanaik (Option 2): An Indian mythologist and author known for books like ‘My Gita’ and ‘Jaya’, but not the author of ‘The Immortals of Meluha’.

 

• Chetan Bhagat (Option 4): A popular Indian author known for novels like ‘Five Point Someone’ and ‘2 States’, not for the Shiva Trilogy.

question: Ain-i Akbari, a document on life of Mughal ruler Akbar does not contain information about ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ancestors.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ain-i-Akbari, written by Abul Fazl (court historian of Akbar), forms the concluding volume of the Akbarnama and provides detailed administrative documentation of Akbar's empire. (आइन-ए-अकबरी — अकबर के प्रशासन का विवरण)

 

• It contains detailed information on the administration (Ain), revenue system, army organisation, geography, culture, and statistics of Akbar's reign, arranged like a gazetteer.

 

• Details about Akbar's ancestors and the narrative history of his reign are instead covered in the earlier volumes (Books I and II) of the Akbarnama, not in the Ain-i-Akbari itself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Akbarnama, commissioned by Akbar, is a three-volume official chronicle of his reign, of which the Ain-i-Akbari is the third and final volume.

 

• The Ain-i-Akbari is considered an invaluable source for understanding Mughal administration, including the mansabdari system and land revenue arrangements.

 

NOTE

 

• Revenues (Option 1): The Ain-i-Akbari extensively documents the empire's revenue system, including land assessment and taxation, so it is covered.

 

• Army (Option 3): The Ain-i-Akbari details the army organisation, including the mansabdari system of military ranks, so it is covered.

 

• Administration (Option 4): Administrative structure and governance form the core subject matter of the Ain-i-Akbari, so it is covered.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct?
I. The property of metals by which they can be beaten into thin sheets is called malleability.
II. The property of metal by which it can be drawn into wires is called ductility.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Malleability is correctly defined in Statement I — it is the property of metals by which they can be beaten (hammered or rolled) into thin sheets. (आघातवर्धनीयता — पत्तियों में बदलने का गुण)

 

• Ductility is correctly defined in Statement II — it is the property of metals by which they can be drawn into thin wires.

 

• Since both statements accurately describe these physical properties of metals, neither statement is incorrect — hence "Neither I nor II" is NOT correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gold and silver are among the most malleable and ductile metals known.

 

• Both malleability and ductility are characteristic physical properties of metals (as opposed to non-metals, which are typically brittle).

 

NOTE

 

• Both I and II (Option 2): Incorrect, since both statements are actually true/correct definitions, not incorrect ones.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement I is a correct (true) definition of malleability, not an incorrect one.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, since Statement II is a correct (true) definition of ductility, not an incorrect one.

question: Chandigarh International Airport has been renamed as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chandigarh International Airport was renamed as the Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport in 2022, in honour of the great freedom fighter and revolutionary Bhagat Singh. (चंडीगढ़ हवाई अड्डा — शहीद भगत सिंह अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डा)

 

• Bhagat Singh was born in Banga village, in Lyallpur district (now in Pakistan's Punjab province), and is closely associated with the Punjab/Chandigarh/Haryana region.

 

• He was executed by the British on 23 March 1931, along with Rajguru and Sukhdev, and is remembered every year on Shaheed Diwas (Martyrs' Day).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhagat Singh, along with Batukeshwar Dutt, threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929 to protest repressive British laws, and was also involved in the killing of British police officer John Saunders in the Lahore Conspiracy Case.

 

• Several other Indian airports have similarly been renamed after freedom fighters and notable figures in recent years.

 

NOTE

 

• Manmohan Singh International Airport (Option 1): Not the new name of Chandigarh airport; Manmohan Singh is a former Prime Minister of India.

 

• Guru Gobind Singh International Airport (Option 3): This is the name of the Bathinda Airport in Punjab, not the Chandigarh airport.

 

• Rajguru International Airport (Option 4): No airport carries this name; Rajguru was a fellow revolutionary executed alongside Bhagat Singh.

question: The Sattriya dance form originated in which of the following Indian States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sattriya is a classical Indian dance form that originated in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) of Assam, introduced by the saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva in the 15th century. (सत्रीया नृत्य — असम की शास्त्रीय नृत्य शैली)

 

• It was traditionally performed by monks in the sattras as a means of religious storytelling, often depicting stories of Radha-Krishna.

 

• Sattriya was officially recognised as one of India's classical dance forms by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in the year 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's eight classical dance forms are: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• Sattriya performances traditionally use musical instruments such as the khol (drum), taal (cymbals), and the flute.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Home to the classical dance form Bharatanatyam, not Sattriya.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Associated with the classical dance form Kathak, not Sattriya.

 

• Manipur (Option 4): Home to the classical dance form Manipuri, not Sattriya.

question: India has won 8 olympic gold medals in which sport till 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Field Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in Field Hockey, in the years 1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, and 1980. (भारत — फील्ड हॉकी में 8 ओलंपिक स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• This makes hockey India's most successful Olympic sport, and India dominated the sport for much of the early-to-mid 20th century.

 

• Legendary hockey player Major Dhyan Chand, often called "The Wizard", was a key figure in three of these gold-medal wins (1928, 1932, 1936).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• After 1980, India did not win another Olympic hockey medal until the Bronze medal at Tokyo 2020, ending a 41-year medal drought.

 

• India's National Sports Day is celebrated on 29 August, the birthday of Major Dhyan Chand.

 

NOTE

 

• Boxing (Option 1): India has won Olympic medals in boxing (e.g., Vijender Singh's bronze in 2008), but no gold medal.

 

• 10m air rifle (Option 3): Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold in 10m air rifle shooting at Beijing 2008, but this is India's only gold in this event, not 8.

 

• Wrestling (Option 4): India has won Olympic medals in wrestling (e.g., Sushil Kumar, Sakshi Malik), but no gold medal in this sport.

question: As of 2022, there are ______ Union Territories of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of 2022, India has 8 Union Territories: Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Delhi (NCT), Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, and Puducherry. (भारत के 8 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश)

 

• The number reduced from 9 to 8 in 2020, when Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were merged into a single Union Territory (effective 26 January 2020).

 

• Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh became separate Union Territories in October 2019, following the reorganisation of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Union Territories are administered directly by the Central Government, generally through an Administrator or Lieutenant Governor appointed by the President.

 

• Delhi (NCT) and Puducherry are Union Territories with their own elected Legislative Assemblies, unlike most other UTs.

 

NOTE

 

• 10 (Option 1): Incorrect; India has never had 10 Union Territories in recent years.

 

• 9 (Option 2): This was the count before the 2020 merger of Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu; no longer correct as of 2022.

 

• 7 (Option 3): Incorrect; understates the actual number of 8 Union Territories as of 2022.

question: The curve giving the maximum amount of corn that can be produced in the economy for any given amount of cotton and vice-versa. This curve is called the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Production possibility frontier.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Production Possibility Frontier (PPF), also called the Production Possibility Curve, shows the maximum possible output combinations of two goods (here, corn and cotton) that an economy can produce with its given resources and technology. (उत्पादन संभावना वक्र)

 

• For any given amount of one good (e.g., cotton), the PPF shows the maximum amount of the other good (corn) that can still be produced, and vice-versa.

 

• The PPF is typically drawn as concave to the origin, reflecting the increasing opportunity cost of shifting resources from producing one good to the other.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Points inside the PPF represent underutilisation of resources, points on the curve represent efficient/maximum production, and points outside the curve are currently unattainable.

 

• The PPF is a fundamental concept in microeconomics used to illustrate scarcity, choice, and opportunity cost.

 

NOTE

 

• Total revenue curve (Option 1): Shows the relationship between total revenue and the quantity of a good sold, unrelated to maximum output combinations of two goods.

 

• Indifference curve (Option 2): Shows combinations of two goods that give a consumer equal satisfaction (utility), not the maximum producible combinations.

 

• Demand curve (Option 4): Shows the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded, not the production trade-off between two goods.
